name: shoemaker
sources: Ó Catháin, Séamus, and Patrick O’Flanagan. The Living Landscape: Kilgallian, Erris, County Mayo. Dublin: Comhairle Bhéaloideas Éireann, 1975, 130.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The shoemaker holds high rank in Irish folklore. A common craftsman rarely gets such honor. The name of the fairy shoemaker, the leprechaun, lifts him. Shoemakers are clever men. Their cleverness can cause trouble. In one tale a man learned shoemaking from the fairies. He made shoes for the parish priest. The priest could not say Mass while he wore them. The fairy shoemaker is Lugh-chromain, the little stooped Lugh. Lugh once ruled the arts and treasure. After Christianization he became a small folklore figure. The leprechaun lives on in books. James Stephens wrote the comic novel Crock of Gold. It became the American musical and film Finian's Rainbow.
